report:
Reviewed the complete recursion_and_fixpoint claim, both ordinary implementation entries, all three substantive tests, and the explicit TODO test. Requirements: directly emitted invocations undergo recursive processing; this is distinct from same-module provisional-member fixed-point recovery; query convergence must not be mistaken for expansion completeness.

Implementation: local_expanded_module_items in local_syms/mods.rs is a Salsa tracked query with an empty cycle_initial. Its ordinary expansion loop calls expand_macro, which resolves the invoked definition, parses its output and directly calls expand_unexpanded_items_at_depth on those emitted items with depth + 1. Nested invocations therefore use explicit recursion rather than treating the next fixed-point iteration as recursive expansion. Recursion is guarded at MAX_EXPANSION_DEPTH. The additional associated resolver file is essential: new_for_macro_expansion creates the macro-expansion phase, resolve_path reaches module lookup, and lookup_in_module reads module.expanded_module_items. The captured ModSymbol wrapper dispatches local modules back to the tracked expansion query. Re-entry into that same query occurs when macro lookup needs provisional members; direct expansion recursion itself does not call cycle recovery. The resolver's separate in_flight list breaks use-chain lookup cycles and is not the expansion fixed point. Fixed-point stability only returns the represented Vec<Symbol>; independent bang_macro_expansion_complete rejects unresolved/ambiguous definitions, errors, active attributes and depth exhaustion, and module_expansion_complete_for_symbol_listing delegates to the conservative completeness traversal. Thus an unchanged vector is not an affirmative completeness certificate.

Tests: same_module_macro_resolution_reaches_a_fixed_point defines a macro that emits another macro definition, then invokes that generated definition as a separate original module invocation. Its assertion finds the Generated struct, detecting failure to revisit provisional same-module members. directly_emitted_invocations_are_expanded instead has outer emit inner! directly and asserts exactly one Generated struct; leaving emitted invocations unprocessed or duplicating their product fails. converged_expansion_can_remain_incomplete queries unresolved missing! twice, observes an empty stable represented member set, and explicitly asserts symbol-listing completeness is false; treating convergence as completeness fails this assertion. Captured fixture helpers create the source-backed local module, specify parsed items and invoke the real expansion query, without hiding assertions.

The semantic_spec TODO is a deferred verification matrix, not a successful behavioral test. Its nested and generated-definition scenarios now have substantive coverage in the tests above, but bounded fixed-point reexecution and warm-cache trace assertions remain deferred. Completing that TODO requires a trace-bearing cold/warm fixture that distinguishes recursive calls from fixed-point reexecution and asserts a bound and stable reuse; these trace properties are not inferred from passing result tests. Keeping that honest TODO is justified and does not claim full query-trace coverage. There are no N/A entries or deferred implementation entries.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing compiler warnings), cargo test -p sage-test-harness same_module_macro_resolution_reaches_a_fixed_point (1 passed), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test macro_fixpoint_review (2 passed). The initial integration-test compile failed because register_tool(sage) was missing; adding the target feature/tool declarations resolved that harness setup issue, with no changed behavioral expectations. Source inspection establishes the structural distinction; the commands establish only the named executed scenarios. The coordinator will run centralized delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks for the association comment and new test file.
